seriesStmt.p: Machine readable texts of the unpublished correspondence of James Joyce

projectDesc.p: James Joyce's unpublished correspondence, collected, annotated, and made available as a digital edition

address.placeName: Chez Francis Grill Room, 7 Place de l'Alma

div.p: As you see the entire typescript has arrived complete. I will try to read it to our friend once more. He wishes me to congratulate you on it – and personally I think it very, very good indeed. We hope your book will be a great success – Don’t you think its success would be a good opportunity for you to organise an exhibition of your pictures?

list.item: Chapelizod: to work in actual names of persons there, from your visit. –
To contrast the easel of an Englishman (Browning, yourself etc) which seems rather otiose with _ _ _

Blake – this element should be worked in much more – in fact Mr Joyce delivered a lecture on Blake in Italian to the Università del Popolo in
Triest Trieste
, the second lecture ever delivered being on Defoe –
Contrast Cain & Abel – to add Ourizen and Luvah

Yeats ’s defence & definition of magic: a) The borders of our minds are always shifting tending to become part of the universal mind b) The borders of our memory – also shift and form part of universal memory c) This universal mind & memory can be evoked by symbols.

div.p: It should be pointed out that Mr J. lived amidst all this (including Yeats) and his library was full of theosophicle theosophical works though he did not use any of the recognised symbols – using instead words trivial and quadrivial and local geographical allusions (Trivial meaning litterally literally – carrefour – where three roads meet).

list.item: Curtail quotations or insert short explanatory sentence less of J. more of yourself –
Speaking of 4 – to mention 4 Zoas in the Blakean sense
Quote your essay in Exagmination about Norse mythology as opposed to Greek – which is almost absent from W.I.P.
Quote a or part of a sonnet of Shakespeare or in fact any old one – towards pg. 20-21 –
Speaking of the importance of the landscape more should be worked in about your art.
The end is a bit brusque.

div.note: In a letter dictated to Paul Léon of 7 May 1933 (LIII 279-80), JJ invited Budgen to send what became chapter 14 of JJMU.
In this and succeeding letters dictated to Léon, JJ provided suggestions to Budgen for his manuscript of JJMU.

In JJMU 310-11 Budgen included a long paragraph from his visit to Chapelizod in which he recounted an afternoon of painting on the south side of the Liffey. He met children who were intrigued by him and his English accent, and later entered the Mullingar Inn for a drink. In the book he reflects that he “made acquaintance with many of the elements of Work in Progress — river, hill, forest, human habitations, laughing girls, brothers in conflict, citizens in council, a woman serving and a big man presiding”.
JJ gave the lectures in March 1912. JJMU ends with Budgen's observations regarding Blake and JJ (318-20).
The Yeats reference is not in the original text of JJMU, but in “Further Recollections of James Joyce”, JJMU 361.
Norse mythology appears in JJMU 312 though the earlier essay is not mentioned.
Part of a Shakespeare sonnet is in JJMU 313.
There is a paragraph on landscape in JJMU 317-18.
